pr_title: Refactor `MaterialStorage::ShaderData` & fix the sorting of shader uniforms
pr_body:
I've detected that several methods in `ShaderData` (`set_path_hint`, `set_default_texture_parameter`, `get_default_parameter`, `get_shader_uniform_list`, `get_instance_param_list`, `is_parameter_texture`) are duplicating across all of its inheritors, which IMO is not good and just waste of space and lead to error-prone hard-detected errors. 

And also I've fixed https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/69949.

issue_context.title: Material Shader Parameters displayed in forced alphabetical order in Inspector
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0 beta 8

### System information

Windows 10 960m

### Issue description

I have noticed when porting a project from 3.5 to 4.0 that shader parameters are now displayed in forced alphabetical order in the inspector. This was not the case in 3.5, where the inspector lists them in the order that they are in the shader script.

When you have a long list of parameters in a custom shader it is normal to want to group them in a logical order for material editing. This is an example of one of my shaders that has 50 or so parameters. As can be see, they are in forced alphabetical order which makes it very hard to edit as they are not grouped in a logical manner. I would tend to put all my maps first, for instance. This forces me to scroll constantly to find what I need to edit.  I do not want to have to rename parameters just to get them in a certain listed order!

![parameter_order](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7741669/207014662-866ee139-d5b4-4d42-a7ff-a793567aef91.jpg)

For the example attached project file this is what it looks like in 4.0 beta 8:

![parameter_order_g4](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7741669/207015217-76336377-f60d-4850-ab28-624035e6022d.jpg)

and the same shader file in 3.5, which shows it in the correct order:

![parameter_order_g3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7741669/207015400-ccef1e96-f9db-4631-9988-d5cbb7b24f09.jpg)




### Steps to reproduce

- Create a new shader material
- Add some uniform parameters
- Look at the inspector to see they have been displayed in alphabetical order

### Minimal reproduction project

[shader_parameter_oder.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10206756/shader_parameter_oder.zip)
comments:
Looks like the alphabetical sorting was added in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/62972 at the same time as uniform groups/subgroups. For shaders with a large number of uniforms I think the intended usage is to organize them into groups as appropriate This gives you control over the organization and lets you fold sections as needed. 

Perhaps @Chaosus can chime in as I am unsure why the alphabetical sorting was added within groups
I need to remember, that part of code I have edited a while ago. I will try to fix it, of course.
@Chaosus  I appreciate you looking into this. Btw, you have done some amazing work on some of the new shader features!

review_comments:
It looks like the bit of code excluding the screen textures was lost in the refactor. 

```suggestion
		if (E.value.scope != ShaderLanguage::ShaderNode::Uniform::SCOPE_LOCAL ||
				E.value.hint == ShaderLanguage::ShaderNode::Uniform::HINT_SCREEN_TEXTURE ||
				E.value.hint == ShaderLanguage::ShaderNode::Uniform::HINT_NORMAL_ROUGHNESS_TEXTURE ||
				E.value.hint == ShaderLanguage::ShaderNode::Uniform::HINT_DEPTH_TEXTURE) {
```

I correctly removed them because they are not added to uniform list of `ShaderData` at the stage of shader compiler:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ec4de82ab322504cf1775fe76fe93e77d5f1f71e/servers/rendering/shader_compiler.cpp#L546-L550

So checking them make no sense.
